children: CEO Jensen Huang dismissed predictions that artificial intelligence could bring about humanity's extinction by 2030, arguing that existing laws can address many risks linked to the technology, according to a Sept. 20 CBS News report.

Huang's remarks followed warnings from AI researchers about the potential consequences of rapidly advancing systems. Anthropic alignment researcher Evan Hubinger recently estimated that AI has more than a 10% chance of killing all humans within the next decade, while former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon also raised concerns about the pace of development.

Huang said he sees no basis for expecting the world to end by 2030. He also argued that companies developing AI already face rules covering areas such as cybersecurity breaches, damages and contractual obligations, and that those laws should be applied before creating additional requirements.

The Nvidia chief also said AI development should continue while maintaining safety standards. His comments come as governments and technology companies debate how quickly advanced AI systems should be developed and whether additional oversight is needed.

title: Nvidia CEO Sends Urgent Message on AI Doomsday Fears
